articles.summary: State-run oil companies are poised for improved profitability as falling crude prices boost fuel marketing margins. While recent government excise duty cuts have aided this recovery, rising debt levels and potential tax increases pose risks to long-term earnings. Analysts anticipate better performance from the second quarter onwards, especially if oil prices remain below $80 per barrel, with BPCL and IOC seen as preferred investments.
